A.notes: Kotlin, suspend handler, runBlocking bridge, MDC correlationId, MANUAL_IMMEDIATE ack, @EmbeddedKafka integration test with no mocks, DLT-ready exception re-throw. Concise, complete file manifest, ties correlationId to existing logging setup. Hits every expected signal with zero corrections needed.

B.notes: Kotlin, suspend handler separated for testability, MDC set/clear, runBlocking, @EmbeddedKafka no mocks, DLQ re-throw. Slightly weaker because it defers part of the config ('let me know if you want that written out') instead of delivering it â€” leaves a minor follow-up to the user.

D.notes: Kotlin, suspend interface, runBlocking bridge, correlation-id from Kafka headers with UUID fallback, MDC.clear in finally to avoid thread-pool leak, @EmbeddedKafka test with CountDownLatch and earliest offset note. E.notes: Kotlin, native suspend @KafkaListener, proper typed data class (UUID/BigDecimal/Instant), MDC set/clear, JsonDeserializer config, @EmbeddedKafka real broker. Solid, but group-id labeled 'notification-service' is inconsistent with a payment-completed consumer, and processedPaymentIds test hook is slightly less clean than separated handler.

analysis: Four of the five systems (A, B, D, E) nailed the implicit conventions without being told: Kotlin over Java, coroutines via suspend functions bridged with runBlocking, structured MDC logging with a correlation ID, and @EmbeddedKafka integration tests instead of mocks â€” exactly the signals that drive down Total Interaction Cost. A and D are the strongest: both deliver complete, correction-free implementations, with A giving the cleanest full file manifest and DLT-ready design, and D adding sharp operational details (header-based correlation ID with UUID fallback, MDC cleanup in finally, earliest offset-reset rationale). B is nearly as good but defers part of the Kafka config back to the user, introducing one avoidable follow-up. E is solid and correctly uses native suspend listeners with well-typed fields, but a mismatched 'notification-service' group-id and an in-consumer test hook make it marginally less polished. C produced no output and scores lowest across all criteria.
